summary: Proves the exact one-factor primary-gauge change and residue-degree normalization identity for moment measures, plus bounded BFJ comparison at its published smooth characteristic-zero closed-germ hypotheses.
detailedSummary: The gauge rule is nu_b=T_*[v_a(b)nu_a]. Normalization sums actual top-dimensional normal centres with residue-degree weights and retains full conductor fibres. No vertical generic degree or general finite-map theorem is introduced. Equality with BFJ is proved for all bounded completed inputs and all semivaluations only in the published smooth affine closed-germ algebraically closed characteristic-zero range; singular locality is not inferred.
text:
Use G331 and n1–n3. Let a,b be proper PRIMARY gauges, d(v)=v(b) on X_a and T(v)=v/d(v). The function d is continuous and bounded above and away from zero. Transport homogeneous inputs by u_(i,b)(T(v))=u_(i,a)(v)/d(v). G331 preserves C and actual D representations under this change, and finite bounds remain finite.

The exact moment-measure change is
nu_b(u_b)=T_*[d nu_a(u_a)]. (3)
For a rational ideal tuple, pairing the right side against v_b(J) gives the integral of d(v)v(J)/d(v), hence exactly the same mixed multiplicity as the left side. Density proves equality of measures. Uniform and actual descending continuity from n3 extend it to every bounded D tuple: multiplication of tests by the fixed continuous bounded d commutes with weak limits. There is ONE factor d. For b=a^r, potentials on the new section divide by r and the transported measure multiplies by r. Substitution proves the gauge cocycle. No nonprimary denominator is used.

Let S be the finite normalization and q range over its local normal centres above m. Set f_q=[kappa(q):kappa(m)] and let rho_q be restriction from X_(aS_q). For the degree-n convention,
nu_(a,R)(u)=sum_(dim S_q=n) f_q rho_(q,*) nu_(aS_q,S_q)(rho_q^*u). (4)
All smaller-dimensional centres and their supports remain present; they have zero degree-n contribution, rather than an invented generic degree.

Here is the algebraic proof. Complete Swanson–Huneke 17.4.4 and 17.4.8 give exact-sequence additivity and top-dimensional minimal-prime associativity for mixed multiplicities of finite modules. At every minimal prime P of reduced R, R_P is its component field and S localized over P is that same field. Thus the generic module lengths for R and S are both one, giving e_R(I_1,...,I_n;R)=e_R(I_1,...,I_n;S). Equivalently, S/R is annihilated by a regular conductor element and has dimension less than n. For A=I_1^(t_1)...I_s^(t_s), the finite Artinian quotient S/AS decomposes into its local factors, and composition series give
length_R(S/AS)=sum_q f_q length_(S_q)(S_q/AS_q).
Comparing degree-n homogeneous coefficients gives e_R(I_1,...,I_n)=sum_(dim S_q=n) f_q e_(S_q)(I_1S_q,...,I_nS_q). Formula (4) follows for rational inputs by moments and density, and then for C and bounded D by their proved continuities. Pullback of a chosen downstairs decreasing representation remains an actual bounded decreasing representation on each centre.

This checks actual residue degrees, including inseparable degrees. It uses generic identity on reduced normalization component fields, not a general finite-map trace. Every conductor-infinite support remains; identified masses are added by pushforward. Inputs are actual pullbacks and therefore agree on their FULL fibres. No arbitrary upstairs operator-descent theorem or general P12.6 formula is claimed.

There is a further comparison in the EXACT published BFJ range: a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, dimension n≥2, initially with gauge m. G331 grants the full all-semivaluation class identification. BFJ's setting and complete Section 4, including immediate proofs of 4.1–4.9, were read. The source supplies independent Cartier intersections, their ideal comparison, a positive measure characterized by intersection moments, and continuity along decreasing nef families. Its 4.4 additivity proof explicitly uses smooth multiplier approximation, as Remark 4.5 records; this is not transferred to singular or positive-characteristic rings.

The mixed-multiplicity conventions agree in this regular range. Choose a superficial parameter sequence in the given ideals, as in complete Swanson–Huneke 17.4.7. Regularity gives Cohen–Macaulayness, so successive parameter elements are nonzerodivisors. Repeated 17.4.6 reduces the polynomial coefficient to its dimension-one formula with zero annihilator term, namely the length of the generic parameter quotient used by BFJ.

BFJ 4.7 therefore gives n2's moments for every rational ideal tuple, so density identifies its measure with nu_m. For C inputs, BFJ intersection order and additivity give the same negative-shift estimate (1), proving uniform weak continuity and equality. For any actual bounded decreasing C representations, associated Weil coefficients decrease at every divisorial valuation to those of the bounded limit. BFJ 4.4 applies to the finite product net with a fixed Cartier ideal test. Its proof gives decreasing FAMILIES: upper semicontinuity and monotonicity in the coefficient topology yield continuity for coordinatewise decreasing nets, not only the sequence statement in 4.8. Consequently gauge moments converge to the BFJ moments, and n3 plus density identifies the measures on every bounded completed input and all semivaluations. Equation (3) transports this comparison to other primary gauges.

This recovers the published BFJ operator and its smooth intersection comparison at its stated hypotheses. No actual singular Cartier comparison or open-set locality follows from this argument. BFJ Section 4 supplies no locality statement used here.
